blocks.content: A driving licence is compulsory for driving any motor vehicle on a public road. Driving without a valid licence is an offence under Section 3 of the MV Act.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Different classifications and categories exist for Driving Licences.
Licence validity dictates the legally permitted operational timeframe before renewal.
Regulatory provisions specify the conditions under which a licence may face suspension or cancellation.

cells: Issued first. Valid for 6 months. Learner must display 'L' board. Must drive with a licensed driver.
Issued after passing driving test. Apply within 30 days of LL but not before 30 days of LL issue.
Trucks, buses — age 20+, must hold LMV licence first

items: Non-transport licence: Valid for 20 years or until age 50, whichever is earlier
Transport vehicle licence: Valid for 3 years (requires medical fitness certificate)
Renew licence before it expires. Driving with expired licence is an offence.
Examine the specific statutory rules governing the different types of driving licences.
Focus on the exact duration and conditions tied to licence validity period regulations.
Memorize the legal grounds and authority clauses under which driving licence suspension or cancellation is enforced.
A licence can be suspended for serious offences like drunk driving, dangerous driving, causing death by negligence, racing on road
Court or licensing authority can cancel a licence
A disqualified person must surrender their licence immediately
